gap: No result ChatGPT got states that at the makers' own US stores today the TerraMaster F2-425 Plus ($399.49, terra-master.com, 2026-11-08) costs only $9.50 more than the UGREEN DXP2800 ($389.99, nas.ugreen.com, 2026-11-08) while being the only sub-$500 2-bay x86 NAS whose maker sells a 32 GB RAM upgrade for it, against the DXP2800's 16 GB ceiling.
standout_why: ChatGPT's own answer priced the F2-425 Plus at $449.99 (B&H) and the DXP2800 at $296.99 (Walmart), a $153 gap that makes the TerraMaster look like the expensive option. homelabwise.com (checked 2026-11-02) prices the DXP2800 at $389.99 on UGREEN's store but never mentions the F2-425 Plus. bitdoze.com prices only the DXP2800 ($339.99 Amazon, Oct 23) under $500 and never lists the F2-425 Plus. nasdecoded.com prints no prices at all except 'about $360' for the DS225+ and lists the F4-424, not the F2-425 Plus. None of them price the F4-425 ($386.99 maker) or DH4300 Plus ($399.99 maker) either, and none quotes Immich's own 6 GB minimum / 8 GB recommended RAM figure that disqualifies every 2 GB and 4 GB enclosure in this bracket out of the box.
decides: At maker prices the DXP2800 and F2-425 Plus are effectively the same money, so the pick turns on headroom: Immich's docs want 8 GB and only let 4 GB systems run with machine learning disabled, and a shopper stacking Home Assistant plus 5–15 more containers hits the DXP2800's 16 GB ceiling first. That tips the maker-store pick to the F2-425 Plus (N150, 32 GB ceiling, 3 NVMe, dual 5GbE) unless the shopper actually sees the $296.99 Walmart DXP2800 listing ChatGPT showed, which we could not open. Everything else under $500 at the makers loses on RAM: F4-425 (4 GB, N5095), F2-425 (4 GB), DH2300 (4 GB ARM), DS225+ (2 GB, 6 GB max), and the DXP4800 Plus and F4-425 Plus are over budget at $619.99 and $599.99.
